propertyEvents.result: Pier Nine: its $1,957,000.00 check, dated June 29, was deposited on July 2, 2026. Cash in transit to HGC at the year end is still a receivable: no misstatement. Kestrel Point: HGC agreed the $28,600.00 credit in writing on June 18, 2026, before the year end, but recorded it in July; revenue and receivables are overstated by it (AR-01), and Kestrel paid $510,000.00, the rest. Brindlewood: the district paid $371,250.00 and keeps $41,250.00 of liquidated damages; HGC has asked for a time extension and recorded nothing. Whether HGC will collect it is a judgment (AR-02).
propertyEvents.locator: Word document; the controller’s notes on credits, disputes and collections of September 4, 2026

tape.label: Kestrel Point Credit Agreed June 18, AR-01

propertyEvents.result: Recompute retainage from each job’s billings and agree it to the replies and the books
propertyEvents.locator: Jun 30 2026!A8:O14; billed to date on each active job, the base for retainage

propertyEvents.result: Retainage at 5% of each active job’s billings to date recomputes to $1,161,125.00, account 1250 to the cent. Three owners confirmed what they hold; Tideflats did not reply, but its $102,500.00 is 5% of the $2,050,000.00 its pay applications billed, and it paid the June billing net of it. Retainage on the jobs completed in the year has been billed for release and sits in contract receivables, where Brindlewood’s difference arose.
propertyEvents.locator: Jun 30 2026!A8:O14; billed to date on each active job, the base for retainage

propertyEvents.result: Test whether an allowance for doubtful accounts is needed
propertyEvents.locator: Word document; the controller’s notes on credits, disputes and collections of September 4, 2026

propertyEvents.result: The client records no allowance and says every contract receivable has been collected except where a credit was agreed (N4). Corliss Medical Group’s $186,935.00 is the exception: it disputes the change order work in the final billing, did not answer the confirmation or three letters, has paid nothing since December, and HGC has filed a lien. The job itself finished at a loss (the job schedule testing’s LOSS-01). A specific allowance of up to $186,935.00 is a judgment for the CPA (AR-03); a lien helps only if the clinic’s property covers it.
propertyEvents.locator: Word document; the controller’s notes on credits, disputes and collections of September 4, 2026

propertyEvents.result: Pier Nine in transit, reconciled · Kestrel credit $28,600 unrecorded · Brindlewood $41,250 withheld · retainage recomputes · Corliss allowance to decide
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $28,600.00, 8.4% of the $340,000.00 materiality (AR-01). The judgments are larger: Brindlewood’s $41,250.00 (AR-02) and the Corliss allowance of up to $186,935.00 (AR-03). Recorded together with AR-01 they come to $256,785.00, more than the $255,000.00 performance materiality, so the CPA weighs them together and with the other FY2026 areas. Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.
